proposals.after: Both men were afraid. That night they climbed the wall to encourage the rampart guards, and in the moonlight plotted their next move. proposals.reason: Chinese 僕射甘言厚德 names Lu Yanhong by office; the idiomatic quote reduces this to an ambiguous 'His'.

proposals.before: Within ten days Wang Jian mustered all the troops Gu Yanlang could spare, raised siege ladders and rams, and assaulted Chengdu. After three days he failed and withdrew, again holding Hanzhou.
proposals.after: Within ten days Wang Jian mustered all the Dongchuan forces, raised siege ladders and rams, and assaulted Chengdu. After three days he failed and withdrew, again holding Hanzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 盡取東川之眾 is the Dongchuan forces, not an explicit naming of Gu Yanlang.

proposals.before: Chen Jingxuan refused to step down. The emperor was furious and ordered Gu Yanlang and Yang Shouliang to attack him. Wei Zhaodu meanwhile made Wang Jian commander of the palace guard and put him in charge of his own troops.
proposals.after: Chen Jingxuan refused to step down. The emperor was furious and ordered Gu Yanlang and Yang Shouliang to attack him. Wei Zhaodu meanwhile made Wang Jian commander of the headquarters troops and put him in charge of his own troops.
proposals.reason: 牙內都校 is an inner yamen / headquarters troop commander, not a palace-guard post.

proposals.before: When Zhao Kuangning lost Jing and Xiang, his younger brother Kuangming fled to Shu with his staff; Jian thereby gained Qí, Xiá, Zhōng, Wàn, and other prefectures.
proposals.after: When Zhao Kuangning lost Jing and Xiang, his younger brother Kuangming fled to Shu with his staff; Jian thereby gained Kui, Xia, Zhong, Wan, and other prefectures.
proposals.reason: The tone-marked Qí misreads 夔 (Kui); the four prefectures are Kuizhou, Xiazhou, Zhongzhou, and Wanzhou, matching the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: When Yan came to Shu, Guangsi and others gave a private banquet and spoke of recent affairs in the central realm; Yan also cited recent events to refute them—the account is in Yan's biography.
proposals.after: When Li Yan came to Shu, Guangsi and others gave a private banquet and spoke of recent affairs in the central realm; Li Yan also cited recent events to refute them—the account is in Li Yan's biography.
proposals.reason: 嚴 here is the envoy Li Yan, not Wang Yan 衍; the literal English collapses both to Yan and makes the biography pointer ambiguous.

proposals.before: Southern forces will march from Jiangling, advancing when the advantage is ours and falling back to hold Xiakou if not.
proposals.after: Southern forces will march from Jiangling, advancing when the advantage is ours and falling back to hold the gorge mouth if not.
proposals.reason: 硤口 names the mouth of the gorges, not the Yangzi city Xiakou (夏口).

proposals.before: I am filled with fear and trembling before Your Majesty, who inherits the legacy of Yao and Shun, marshals armies like those of the Shang founders, pacifies the realm, destroys the wicked, gathers tribute from every quarter, and unifies the empire under one order.
proposals.after: I am filled with fear and trembling before Your Majesty, who inherits the legacy of Yao and Shun, marshals armies like those of Tang and Wu, pacifies the realm, destroys the wicked, gathers tribute from every quarter, and unifies the empire under one order.
proposals.reason: 湯、武 are Tang of Shang and King Wu of Zhou, not a single pair of Shang founders.

proposals.before: When Wang Jian declared himself emperor, Hanlin academicians received the greatest favor. Some courtiers said his courtesies went too far. Wang Jian replied, "You simply have not seen how it was done before.
proposals.after: When Wang Jian declared himself emperor, only the Hanlin academicians received the greatest favor. Some courtiers said his courtesies went too far. Wang Jian replied, "You simply have not seen how it was done before.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 惟 restricts the exceptional favor to Hanlin academicians; the idiomatic English omits that limiter, which the literal already preserves.

proposals.before: When Meng Zhixiang took command of Shu, Chang and his mother entered Shu together with his wife, the Eldest Princess of Qionghua.
proposals.after: When Meng Zhixiang took command of Shu, Chang and his mother entered Shu together with Zhixiang's wife, the Eldest Princess of Qionghua.
proposals.reason: Chinese 從知祥妻瓊華長公主 makes the princess Meng Zhixiang's wife; after naming Chang, English his wife wrongly reads as Chang's wife.

decisions.reason: The spoken line addresses Lu Yanhong as 僕射, not with a pronoun. Reducing that office to 'His' omits the title used in the quote, even though s0010 already makes the feigned favors his.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 僕射甘言厚德，是疑我也

decisions.reason: The sentence says Jian took all the forces of Dongchuan (東川之眾). It does not name Gu Yanlang; inserting him invents an agent this unit does not state.
牙內都校 is a governor-headquarters command, not a palace-guard post. 'Commander of the headquarters troops' corrects that error without changing the rest of the sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時昭度以建為牙內都校，董其部兵

decisions.reason: The same 牙內都校 is mistranslated as palace guard in the literal. 'Inner yamen commander' matches the office name and the following 董其部兵.
The Chinese annotation closer 〉 after 行府。） is markup, not English. The English already closes with a parenthesis; the trailing 〉 should be dropped.
The literal likewise copies the annotation closer 〉 after a complete English parenthesis. Removing only that leaked mark is correct.
The unit ends 餓死。」）〉. English already has the closing quote and parenthesis that match s0062; only the leaked 〉 is extraneous.
Same annotation leak in the literal: keep the English ") that closes the Shu Annals quotation, and drop only 〉.
夔 is Kui, not Qí. 峽、忠、萬 are Xia, Zhong, and Wan, matching the idiomatic Kuizhou, Xiazhou, Zhongzhou, and Wanzhou.
Each 嚴 in this unit is the envoy Li Yan (李嚴), including 語在嚴傳. Bare 'Yan' collides with Wang Yan 衍 in the surrounding narrative.
硤口 is the mouth of the gorges (峽/硤), a fallback west of Jiangling toward Shu, not the Yangzi city 夏口 (Xiakou).
湯、武 names Tang of Shang and King Wu of Zhou as paired martial exemplars. 'Shang founders' drops Wu and misassigns him to Shang.
惟 restricts the exceptional favor to the Hanlin academicians. Omitting 'only' lets the sentence mean they merely ranked high among others so favored.
知祥妻 is Meng Zhixiang's wife, the Eldest Princess of Qionghua. After naming Chang, 'his wife' wrongly makes her Chang's spouse.
